reform_contract._comment: W1's runner (policyengine.py#577); its pass also needs policyengine-uk#2305 and policyengine.py#575, so certified 2.125.1 fails the dated cases by design.

tool._comment: W3's aggregate-impact tool, pinned so both pairs use the same definitions: the approved head of draft policyengine-uk#2335. It suppresses figures from fewer than 10 records and gives each total's excluded figures with their signs (exclude_signs), which the metrics review requires. #2335 merges after cos d1601; move the pin to the merged commit when it lands, and never to a commit without suppression.

reform_responsiveness._comment: Plan invariant 'Reform responsiveness' (11 Oct 2026): a reform the model silently ignores must fail qualification. The standard set, each reform's target variable, direction and yearly minimum are the metrics tool's own (standard_reforms.yaml in the pinned tool; at 228a05a3e each minimum is a fifth of the reform's smallest yearly effect on the certified pair, adopted under cos d1344). The tool costs the set by default and emits reform_runs:<id> and responsive:<id> checks. This gate requires both checks to be present and passing for every standard reform in the candidate's report, and recomputes each responsive verdict from the report's reform_targets.<id> values.

promotion.decision: cos d1344 (15 October 2026): automatic promotion is on once policyengine.py#574 lands on its gates. The promote job fast-forwards main to the newest promotable candidate's qualified commit once every check on it has passed, which succeeds only while main is still the commit the candidate was built on; otherwise the candidate is requalified on current main. A needs-review receipt is promoted only after a named reviewer accepts that exact receipt.
